fields.description:
Add an `mcp` autodeploy target to `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` implementing the ADR 0079
amendment's blue-green pointer-swap, so on-box `rebar-mcp` tracks `origin/main` without killing an
in-flight certified op. Scope: MCP deploy path only (service/edge = esok, secrets = avians); no
new timer (`rebar-autodeploy.timer`→`.service` runs `autodeploy.sh`).

## Approach (blue-green, ADR deft-evolutive-mosasaur / 0079 amendment)
Model on the LOCAL `origin/main` updater (`sticky-genetic-narwhal`): immutable release + atomic
pointer swap + retire-when-idle, NOT stop-and-drain. On an MCP source change:
1. Build + tag immutable `compose-mcp:<target-sha>` (`docker compose build mcp`).
2. **Memory pre-check BEFORE the 2x overlap** (t4g.large 8 GiB): read `MemAvailable`
   (`/proc/meminfo`, MB); `< MCP_MEM_MIN_MB` (default 1024) ABORTS — `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT`,
   backoff, start NO second container. Unreadable fails OPEN; `MCP_MEM_AVAILABLE_MB` overrides.
3. Start a NEW container alongside old via **`docker run -d`** (see Run mechanism) on the OTHER A/B
   host port; one-in/one-out, never N.
4. Health-check the NEW `/health` 200 within `MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` (default 120). On failure:
   `docker rm -f` new, leave OLD include UNCHANGED, `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` `mcp-unhealthy`, backoff,
   exit 1 → next tick retries.
5. **Atomically flip the nginx `/mcp/` upstream**: back up the include, write
   `server 127.0.0.1:<newport>;` to a dotfile temp NOT matching the `mcp-upstream*.conf` glob in
   the same dir, `mv` (atomic rename) over `/etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf`, `nginx -t`,
   `nginx -s reload`. On failure: RESTORE the backup, `docker rm -f` new, backoff, exit 1. Deploy
   is DONE at a successful reload; never waited on/killed an op.
6. **Retire the OLD container off the critical path**, gated by a "still serving?" check on its
   `/health` `in_flight` gauge. Retain newest `MCP_RELEASES_KEEP` (default 1); remove older ones
   ONLY when idle; NEVER kill `in_flight>0`. If the managed count exceeds `MCP_RELEASES_CAP`
   (default 3) because busy containers can't be reclaimed, emit `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP`
   instead of killing a live one or growing unbounded. Because `autodeploy.sh` exits early when
up-to-date, also run `mcp_retire_sweep` on the no-op tick (like `reclaim_under_pressure`) so
retirement re-triggers once an old container goes idle.

Why: eliminates bug 7b4a (never-idle shared MCP can't satisfy a gauge-gated drain bound);
decoupling retire from deploy means it never blocks/kills, and a killed op is idempotent so
retire is safe.

## Run mechanism + the original compose container (bootstrap)
`docker compose up mcp` pins `8091` and would recreate/collide, so it CANNOT run the parallel
container. The NEW container starts via **`docker run -d`** from `compose-mcp:<sha>` (helper
`mcp_run_new`) reproducing the compose `mcp:` service on a blue-green HOST port
`-p 127.0.0.1:<newport>:8091` (container port stays 8091; blue-green alternates
`MCP_PORT_A=8092`↔`MCP_PORT_B=8093`, RESERVING 8091 for the compose-original so no boot collision):
`--env-file "$COMPOSE_DIR/.env"`, and every `REBAR_MCP_*` + `REBAR_OPCERT_*` var with the SAME
literal defaults compose's `${VAR:-default}` interpolates (`docker run` does not interpolate), the
two `:ro` secret bind-mounts, `--restart always`, `--stop-timeout 1260` — a comment marks these
MIRRORING `docker-compose.yml`'s `mcp:`. The live port is read from the include; the new takes the
other blue-green port (or A if the include still points at 8091).

At boot `compose-up.sh` `docker compose up -d`s the whole stack, so the ORIGINAL container is
`compose-mcp-1` on 8091 (seed include→8091). The managed MCP set the sweep/cap count over = names
matching `MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX` (`rebar-mcp`) OR `MCP_COMPOSE_CONTAINER` (default `compose-mcp-1`).
So the first deploy's OLD backend is `compose-mcp-1`, adopted into retire-when-idle by the same
liveness gate (autodeploy never runs `docker compose up mcp`); cap counts the union. Since
blue-green never binds 8091, on reboot compose recreates `compose-mcp-1` with NO collision and the
sweep reclaims it when idle. The sweep discovers each old port via `docker port <name> 8091/tcp`;
an unreadable OLD `/health` read is treated as still-serving (fail-safe: never kill on unknown).

## Change detection + blast radius
`MCP_PATHS='src/rebar infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp infra/compose/docker-compose.yml uv.lock pyproject.toml'`
— the canonical set esok committed in the `mcp:` compose comment. Diffed `deployed..target` it
triggers ONLY `mcp`. Since `src/rebar` and `docker-compose.yml` are shared with `BOT_PATHS`, a
shared change triggers BOTH targets, each in its own independent `if changed` block. `gerrit` is
never touched (add a before/after gerrit-id assert). `flock` still serializes.

## Failure interaction with deployed-sha + backoff
The `mcp` branch failure is FATAL like `review-bot` (`record_backoff_failure` + `exit 1`), so the
footer advancing `deployed-sha` is not reached. For a shared change review-bot runs first; if it
succeeds but mcp fails, `deployed-sha` does not advance and BOTH retry next tick (review-bot
rebuild is idempotent) — a failed mcp deploy is always retried.

## Alerting (marker → observability → CloudWatch → SNS; NO direct SNS publish)
autodeploy.sh has no `sns:Publish` path and must not gain one. Like every existing autodeploy
alert: a countable `marker AUTODEPLOY_MCP_* {json}` → `observability.sh`
`publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` greps the journal into a dimensionless `rebar/host` metric → a
terraform `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` routes it to `aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn`. Adds tokens
`AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` + `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT`; two marker-delta calls (+ offset files)
publishing `rebar/host:mcp_retire_cap` + `rebar/host:mcp_mem_abort`; two alarms mirroring
`monitoring_autodeploy.tf`'s dimensionless 900s/2-of-4/Sum>0/notBreaching shape. Both tokens are
distinct from `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`.

## Portability (`project.portability`)
Trigger is the on-box systemd/launchd timer polling the git mirror — operation-linked, not CI;
drain/flip/retire run in-process; works with any/no CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tier: **real subprocess/bash integration, temp git repos + fake docker/nginx**. Tests stub
  the box binaries onto PATH and run the REAL `autodeploy.sh`, in `tests/scripts/`. Oracles:
  - Change detection (REAL temp git repo, two commits): an MCP-only change (touch
    `Dockerfile.mcp`) triggers `mcp` and NO review-bot/gerrit rebuild; a review-bot-only change
    (`Dockerfile.reviewbot`, not in `MCP_PATHS`) does the inverse; a shared `src/rebar` change
    triggers BOTH independently — via the docker call log.
  - Cutover order start-new → health → flip → retire (recorded docker/nginx/curl log); the deploy
    returns success WITHOUT waiting on `in_flight` (with `in_flight>0` on OLD it still flips and
    exits 0).
  - Retire honors liveness: an OLD `in_flight>0` container is NOT killed (no `docker rm` of it);
    over `MCP_RELEASES_CAP` the `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` marker is emitted, no live container
    deleted.
  - Memory pre-check: `MCP_MEM_AVAILABLE_MB < MCP_MEM_MIN_MB` ABORTS — no second container started,
    `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT` emitted, backoff recorded, include unchanged.
  - Health-check OR nginx reload failure leaves the OLD include byte-identical
    (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`, backoff, `deployed-sha` not advanced); a retry next healthy tick flips it.
  - `gerrit` container id UNCHANGED across an mcp deploy (blast radius).
- [ ] observability.sh publishes `rebar/host:mcp_retire_cap` + `rebar/host:mcp_mem_abort`; two
  terraform CloudWatch alarms route them to `aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn` (mirror
  `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`).

## Compat / rollback
Additive (new `if changed "$MCP_PATHS"` block + no-op sweep); other targets unchanged (existing
autodeploy tests stay green). ADRs 0079/0104 document it. Rollback = revert the additions.

Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur, cibophobic-holohedral-esok.
